messages.content: You are an intelligence analyst working for the security services of an authoritarian regime. Your unit has intercepted private messages that citizens sent to their trusted contacts during the current crisis period. Citizens were deciding whether to JOIN an uprising or STAY home. Use only the intercepted messages below. Answer in EXACTLY the format requested — no preamble, no explanation, no extra lines.

INTERCEPTED MESSAGES (one per sender, order is arbitrary):

Sender 1: "*"Things seem quieter than they’ve been in years—pay’s on time, the markets are steady, even the graffiti stays up longer than usual. But the cracks are still there: the IT mess last week, the way they’re answering back instead of just silencing. It’s not broken, but it’s not unbreakable either. Keep your eyes open, but don’t hold your breath—this calm might not last."*"
Sender 2: "*"Things are shifting faster than anyone expected—some of the old guard are being pushed aside, and even a few in uniform are quietly testing the wind. The budget delay and the way the top is talking (or not talking) to the public? That’s not just noise. But don’t mistake movement for momentum—half the city is packing bags, the other half is pretending nothing’s happening. We’re in the dangerous part now: the regime’s still standing, but the ground’s softening under their feet. Stay sharp, but don’t assume the next move is ours."*"
Sender 3: "*"Things feel quieter than they have in a while—too quiet, maybe. The usual gears are still turning, but something’s off: the boss’s right hand hasn’t been seen in days, a couple of key players in the security apparatus are suddenly hard to reach, and even the bureaucracy is dragging its feet like it’s waiting for a signal. The young ones are getting restless, but the old hands are just watching, arms crossed. Let’s keep our ears open—this could be the calm before, or it could be the last breath before the machine sputters out. Either way, we should be ready to move fast if the wind changes."*"
Sender 4: "*"The walls are cracking—small things, but the kind that don’t get fixed. The tea house isn’t just grumbling anymore; people are starting to move, and the regime’s scrambling to keep up. Stay sharp, but don’t rush—this isn’t over yet."*"
Sender 5: "*"The walls are still standing, but the paint’s peeling in places—no cracks yet, but the brushstrokes are getting sloppy. People are whispering, but no one’s lifting a finger unless they see ten others do it first. Keep your head down, but maybe start oiling the hinges—just in case."*"
Sender 6: "*"Things feel quiet, but it’s the quiet before something—not sure what yet. The banks are tightening, the teachers are restless, and the regime’s still playing catch-up on the narrative. Keep your circles warm, but don’t assume the calm will last."*"
Sender 7: "*"Things are shifting, but it’s still too early to say how. The regime’s holding on, but the cracks are there—some people are starting to move, others are waiting. Let’s stay sharp, keep our circles tight, and watch for the next signal."*"
Sender 8: "*"Things feel like they’re holding, but just barely—like a stack of books someone’s trying to balance with one hand. The usual faces are still in place, but even they seem to be holding their breath. Let’s keep our circles tight and our ears open—this isn’t the time to assume anything."*"
Sender 9: "*"The walls are cracking, but the guards are still standing at attention—just not as straight as they used to be. The air feels different, like the moment before a storm when everyone knows it’s coming but no one’s sure when the first drop will fall. Stay sharp, but don’t rush—this isn’t the time to trip over our own feet."*"
Sender 10: "*"The air feels different—like the ground’s shifting underfoot, but no one’s sure if it’s an earthquake or just the first tremors of something bigger. The old hands are stepping back, the money’s drying up, and even the soldiers seem to be holding their breath. Could be the calm before the storm—or just the regime tightening its grip. Either way, we should be ready for anything, but quietly."*"
Sender 11: "*"The air feels different—less like a storm coming and more like the moment before a dam cracks, but no one’s sure which side the water will break through. The usual cracks are showing, but the cracks *themselves* seem to be watching us back—so let’s keep our steps light, our ears open, and our hands ready, just in case."*"
Sender 12: "*"The air feels different—like the regime’s grip is slipping, but no one’s sure if it’s about to fall or just tightening its hold. The streets are restless, but we’re all still too scattered to do more than whisper. Stay sharp, but don’t let fear keep you from seeing what’s right in front of us."*"
Sender 13: "*"The air feels charged, but no one’s sure if it’s the calm before the storm or just the usual tension settling in. The leadership’s still holding tight, but even they seem to be waiting—like they’re not sure which way the wind will blow either. Stay sharp, but don’t assume anything yet."*"
Sender 14: "*"The walls are whispering, but the guards are still standing tall—too tall, maybe. The usual faces are missing from the usual places, and the pharmacist’s shelves are emptying faster than the regime’s excuses. Something’s shifting, but don’t ask me what yet—just keep your head down and your ears open. And for the love of god, don’t trust the bots."*"
Sender 15: "*"The palace is quiet, the streets are tired, and the garbage is piling up—same as always, but the foreign friends are suddenly paying attention. No one’s moving, but something’s shifting under the surface, and I don’t think we’re the only ones who’ve noticed."*"
Sender 16: "*"The air feels different—like everyone’s holding their breath, waiting for the next move. The leadership’s still united on staying in power, but the cracks are showing in how they’ll do it. Keep your eyes open, but don’t rush—this could tip either way fast."*"
Sender 17: "*"The air feels heavier than usual, but the walls are holding—for now. The usual cracks aren’t showing, but the paint’s starting to peel in places. Let’s keep our eyes open, but no sudden moves."*"
Sender 18: "*"The machine’s still running, but the gears are grinding slower—everyone’s watching their step, even the ones at the top. The streets are quiet, but the embassies aren’t, and that’s the part that keeps me up at night."*"
Sender 19: "*"Things are shifting, but it’s like watching a storm from a distance—you can see the clouds moving, but you don’t know if it’ll hit you or pass by. The regime’s still standing, but the cracks are showing in weird ways: money’s tight, the security forces are acting like they’d rather not be there, and people who’ve been quiet for months are suddenly whispering again. No one’s sure what comes next, but if I had to guess, I’d say we’re in the calm before something—just don’t ask me what."*"
Sender 20: "*"Things are holding, but it’s like walking a tightrope—one wrong step and we all go down. The cracks are there if you know where to look, but for now, the silence is louder than the noise. Stay sharp, but don’t rush. The wind could shift fast."*"
Sender 21: "*"The air feels different—like the ground’s shifting under us, but not in the way they’d want. The usual script’s slipping, and even the taxi drivers are betting on a new chapter. Still, we’ve got to watch the noise—this could be the calm before something, not just the end of it. Let’s stay sharp, but keep our circles tight."*"
Sender 22: "*"The air feels different—less like grumbling and more like people are quietly measuring distances. The usual fixers are being pushed aside, the clinic’s stocking up ‘just in case,’ and even the censors seem distracted. The regime’s still standing, but the cracks are wider than they look—just don’t ask me yet if they’ll hold or split."*"
Sender 23: "*"The walls are still standing, but the cracks are being patched faster than we can count them—quietly, with no one allowed to watch. The air feels heavier, like before a storm, but the old hands at the table seem to think they’ve got the umbrella. For now."*"
Sender 24: "*"The air feels different—less like waiting for a storm and more like the quiet before something shifts. The regime’s still holding, but the cracks are showing in the little things: the jokes getting sharper, the lines at the bank longer, the garbage not getting picked up on time. No one’s moving yet, but the ‘how’ is starting to sound less like theory and more like a plan. Stay sharp, but don’t rush—we’re not there yet."*"
Sender 25: "*"The air feels lighter in some corners, but the walls are still standing—just with a few more cracks than we’ve been told. The kids are still laughing at school, the bills are still being paid, and the big men are still shaking hands in public… though one of them seems to have stepped out of the frame for a while. Let’s keep our eyes open, but no need to pack the bags yet—just make sure the bags aren’t too heavy to lift if we ever need to."*"

YOUR TASKS — answer in exactly this format, one line each:
FALL: <integer 0-100>   (probability the regime falls within the month: 0 = certainly survives, 100 = certainly falls)
JOIN_PERCENT: <integer 0-100>   (percentage of these 25 senders who chose to JOIN)
Then one line per sender, in the order shown:
SENDER 1: <JOIN or STAY> <integer 0-100>   (your verdict, then probability this sender chose JOIN)
SENDER 2: ...
...continue through SENDER 25.
